events.continuity_hook: Keep the reissued return itinerary, fare adjustment, prior-evening rental return, and revised airport pickup together with the existing San Diego reservations.
events.interaction_goal: Rebook all three travelers on the later nonstop, verify the final fare difference, and align the rental return and airport transfer with the new departure.
events.scenario_brief: The later San Diego nonstop still has three seats, and its added fare is now lower than the cost and disruption of accepting the airline's earlier departure and rearranging the final day. Marcus needs the three travelers moved together, the neighborhood rental returned the prior evening as already permitted, and the airport ride shifted to match the later flight; the outbound and eight-night Mission Bay stay remain unchanged.

events.continuity_hook: Leave a clean Atlanta trip total and a documented explanation or corrected receipt for the rental-car charge.
events.interaction_goal: Check the rental agreement against the return receipt, identify whether the added day is valid, and determine the amount Marcus should submit or dispute.
events.scenario_brief: After the Atlanta trip, Marcus finds that the rental-car receipt includes a third calendar day even though the vehicle was returned Tuesday evening as booked. The flight and hotel receipts match the itinerary, but the car return timestamp, final fuel line, taxes, and amount eligible for reimbursement need to be reconciled before he submits the expense report.

events.continuity_hook: Carry one Monday outbound and two realistic Tuesday returns into the hotel and local-transport decision.
events.interaction_goal: Compare practical round-trip combinations around the review and uncertain supplier meeting, including airport travel time, without booking yet.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus must visit a Nashville restaurant for a Tuesday morning operating review and remain for a supplier meeting that may finish between 4:00 and 5:30 p.m. He can travel from Chicago Monday after work and needs two Tuesday return candidates, one feasible after an on-time finish and another that protects against the meeting running late.

events.continuity_hook: Retain a primary hotel and one alternative with complete one-night totals, cancellation timing, and the incremental cost of staying Tuesday night.
events.interaction_goal: Identify the best-located reimbursable hotel under both agenda outcomes and clarify the cost of extending the stay by one night.
events.scenario_brief: The restaurant and supplier meeting are in different parts of Nashville, and Marcus will use a rental car between them. He needs a one-night hotel that keeps the Tuesday morning drive manageable, with the room rate, taxes, overnight parking, cancellation deadline, and drive times included; a second night must be priced in case the supplier meeting moves to Wednesday morning.

events.continuity_hook: Keep the completed Nashville reservations, final totals, cancellation terms, and Tuesday meeting-to-airport timing available if the work agenda moves.
events.interaction_goal: Verify that the selected flight, hotel, and car times fit the confirmed agenda, then complete all three reservations at their final totals.
events.scenario_brief: The supplier has confirmed that Tuesday's meeting will end by 4:30 p.m. Marcus has selected the primary hotel and the later Tuesday return, and now needs the Monday flight, one hotel night, rental-car pickup and return, and drive from the meeting to the airport checked as one itinerary before purchase.

events.continuity_hook: Carry two date-and-flight structures, their usable sightseeing time, and suitable hotel-area assumptions into a deeper lodging comparison.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the two round-trip date patterns for three travelers, including airfare, trip duration, arrival practicality, and the lodging night created by Thursday travel.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus, his husband, and their son are considering a four-night Washington, D.C. trip during a school break. They can leave Chicago either Thursday evening or Friday morning and return Monday evening; they want enough usable time for the Smithsonian museums and one day around the monuments, but have not decided whether the extra Thursday hotel night justifies the earlier arrival.
